title: Variance decomposition
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, and let $f$ be real-valued on its outcome space. Its variance is the sum of the expected squared components over all nonempty coordinate subsets: $\operatorname{Var}_P(f)=\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}\mathbb E_P[f_S^2]$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses
$f$ is real-valued on the outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ with orthogonal components $f_S$. Then $\operatorname{Var}_P(f)=\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq[n]}\mathbb E_Pf_S^2$.
